evidence: REACHABILITY. Every capability the brief asks for is reachable from the seed plus the pinned runtime; none needs the network. (1) Runtime: instruction.md:13 asks for Node.js, Express and SQLite with 'Server dependencies are already available, so don't install packages'. environment/Dockerfile:9-12 and tests/Dockerfile:16-22 both install express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 globally with NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules. test.sh:106-110 launches with NODE_PATH, PORT=3000 and DB_PATH, matching instruction.md:13 and hireops_rules.md:198-202, which warn about a different working directory and a copied app. (2) Live updates: rules:123 allow 'Polling, server-sent events and sockets', so polling or SSE works with Express and Node built-ins and needs no ws package. Sessions, password checks and IDs need only Node built-ins (crypto). Drafts can use browser storage or the server ('Where drafts are kept is yours', rules:175). (3) Seed: instruction.md:15 says to copy what is needed into /app because /assets and /instructions are unavailable at runtime. The seed holds everything a criterion relies on: 10 users matching instruction.md:17 and app_context.md; 3 jobs with interview_limit; 16 applications with stage and position (Platform Engineer Applied Greta/Ade/Marco and Screen Priya/Samuel, as hro_restart expects); Noor's note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.'; 127 messages, of which APP-101 has 120 with sorted, unique timestamps; read markers; candidate_status_labels; thread_page_size=30. I recomputed the seeded expectations. Lena (USR-CAN3) has read_count 2 on APP-301, whose 3rd message is from USR-REC3, giving exactly 1 unread, as functional prompt Z and hro_unread_counts state. Noor has read_count 119 of 120, and the 120th message is her own. Rafael has read 120. (4) Network: the public sheet and the SKILL delivery profile say network is allowed. The Internal sheet annotation says 'no network'. That conflict does not matter here because nothing in the brief needs the network; integration.md:12-14 only permits CDN assets in the browser. (5) Measured support: raw-evidence-index.json artifact hashes and matching_source_files all re-hash equal to the frozen solution. results/workspace.json records 25 scripted golden groups passing as uid 65534 with a real restart. These cover stale 409 naming who, bulk all-or-nothing, undo rules, roles 401/403/404, paging, unread and seen, drafts, live board within 804 ms, and candidate privacy. That shows the brief can be built in this environment. It is scripted evidence, not a configured judge, Oracle or model score. UNAMBIGUITY. I compared each graded scenario with the rules and found one reasonable reading for each. Out-of-date moves: rules:77-80 require a per-card version that changes on every move, so the protocol C replay of 'Applied->Screen' after Mei moved F back to Applied must be refused. An app that only compares the from-stage would accept it, and the rules plainly exclude that design. Undo: rules:96-100 settle the tested cases: a note does not count, another card's change does not count, a re-order or reject of the moved card blocks undo, and only one undo is allowed. I traced protocol B steps 1-15 against those rules, and every expected order follows from rules:89-92 board order. One reading is open: whether a person's own re-order supersedes an earlier move for undo. No protocol puts a re-order between a move and its undo (B(3) comes before B(4) and B(5) undoes B(4)), so it is never exercised. Refusal statuses: rules:21-23 give 401 for no session, 403 for a role that does not reach, and 404 only for a candidate. Candidate wording comes from rules:183-190 and the seed labels. Paging and remaining count come from rules:144-147, and unread and seen from rules:151-166. Draft persistence across sign-out and another user (hro_pol_session_resume) is fixed by instruction.md:7 ('...or get signed out; when I sign back in it is still there, and nobody else who signs in on that browser sees it') and by rules:106 for notes ('kept for that person on that browser until it is saved'). NOTES (non-blocking; reported per the row's 'report every ambiguity' duty): (a) The 'invalid address' in hro_add_email_rules is not named, and rules:32 says only 'must look like an email address'. If a grader picked a borderline value like 'a@b', a lenient but reasonable validator could be marked down. (b) The brief and rules assume a refused move can be attempted (instruction.md:3, rules:82-85). A UI that disables 'move to Interview' when the board already shows Interview full is allowed by the prompt's 'whether a refused action is offered is the app's choice'. hro_refused_put_back also accepts a UI that refuses before the card moves only with a reason shown and focus on that card, and a disabled control cannot take focus. This is mainly a criterion-fairness question for the rows that own it; the public reading still points to attempt-and-refuse. (c) The Internal sheet's 'no network' wording conflicts with the public sheet and the skill. It has no effect here. (d) Unread for a staff member with no seeded read marker on a seeded conversation is defined only by the general rule at rules:151-153 (no marker means never opened, so all messages by others are unread). Only relative changes are graded, so this does not affect any criterion. COUNTERFACTUALS. Broken apps that could pass: none found that the ambiguities above would let through. Apps that compare from-stage, clear drafts on sign-out or have no card versions all break a rule that is stated, and the matching criteria catch them. Conforming alternatives that could fail: note (b), a pre-disabled full-Interview control, is the most plausible, and the risk is low because a stale board must still handle server refusals.
suggested_fix: Optional, non-blocking. Name the invalid address in hro_add_email_rules / protocol S (for example 'not-an-email'). For hro_refused_put_back, say how a pre-disabled control with a visible reason is judged. Neither change is required for this row to pass.
